source_text: Huic expeditissimae probationi defensio quoque a nobis necessaria est aduersus obstrepitacula diuersae partis. aiunt enim Marcionem non tam innouasse regulam separatione legis et euangelii quam retro adulteratam recurasse. o Christe, patientissime domine, qui tot annis interuersionem praedicationis tuae sustinuisti, donec tibi scilicet Marcion subuenirct! nam et ipsum Petrum ceterosque, columnas apostolatus, a Paulo reprehensos opponunt, quod non recto pede incederent ad euangelii ueritatem, ab illo certe Paulo, qui adhuc in gratia rudis, trepidans denique, ne in uacuum currisset aut curreret, tunc primum cum antecessoribus apostolis conferebat. igitur si feruenter adhuc, ut neophytus, aduersus Iudaismum aliquid in conuersatione reprehendendum existimauit, passiuum scilicet (uindicans) conuictum, postmodum et ipse usu omnibus omnia futurus, ut omnes lucraretur, Iudaeis quasi Iudaeus et eis, qui sub lege, tamquam in lege, tu illam solius conuersationis, placiturae postea accusatori suo, reprehensionem suspectam uis haberi etiam de praedicationis erga deum praeuaricatione. atquin de praedicationis unitate. quod supra legimus, dexteras iunxerant, et ipsa officii distributione de euangelii societate condixerant. sicut et alibi: siue ego, inquit, siue illi, sic praedicamus. sed et si quosdam falsos fratres inrepsisse descripsit, qui uellent Galatas ad aliud euangelium transferre, ipse demonstrat adulterium illud euangelii non ad alterius dei et Christi fidem transferendam, sed ad disciplinam legis conseruandam habuisse intentionem, deprehendens scilicet illos circumcisionem uindicantes et obseruantes tempora et dies et menses et annos Iudaicarum caerimoniarum, quas iam exclusas agnouisse debuerant, secundum innouatam dispositionem creatoris olim de hoc ipso praedicantis per prophetas suos, ut per Esaiam: uetera transierunt. inquit, ecce noua, quae ego nunc facio. sic et per Hieremiam: et disponam testamentum, non quale disposui ad patres uestros, cum illos eduxissem de terra Aegypti; et alibi: renouate uobis nouamen nouum, et circumcidimini deo uestro, et circumcidimini praeputia cordis uestri. hanc ergo circumcisionem iam sistens apostolus et hoc nouamen, illas quoque uetustates caerimoniarum dissuadebat, de quibus idem conditor earum quandoque cessaturis profitebatur per Osee: et auertam omnes iocunditates eius et dies festos eius et neomenias et sabbata et omnes caerimonias eius. sic enim et per Esaiam: neomenias uestras et sabbata et diem magnum non sustineo, ferias et ieiunium et dies festos uestros odit anima mea. quodsi et creator omnia haec iam pridem recusauerat et apostolus ea iam recusanda pronuntiabat, ipsa sententia apostoli consentanea decretis creatoris probat non alium deum ab apostolo praedicatum quam cuius decreta cupiebat iam agnosci, falsos et apostolos et fratres notans in hac causa, qui euangelium Christi creatoris transferrent a nouitate praenuntiata a creatore ad uetustatem recusatam a creatore.\'
pass_a_gloss: To this very expedient proof, a defense is also necessary from us against the clamors of the diverse party. For they say that Marcion did not so much innovate the rule by separating the law and the gospel, as he recalled a rule that had been previously adulterated. Oh Christ, most patient Lord, who for so many years endured the perversion of your preaching, until Marcion would come to your aid! For they also oppose Peter and the other pillars of apostleship, who were rebuked by Paul, because they were not walking uprightly to the truth of the gospel, by that same Paul, who was still unpolished in grace, and was trembling, lest he had run or would run in vain, when he first conferred with the preceding apostles. Therefore, if he, still fervent as a new convert, considered something in their conversation to be reprehensible against Judaism, then, having been convinced, he would later become all things to all men, so that he might gain all, to the Jews as a Jew, and to those who were under the law, as under the law, you have that rebuke of conversation, which would please his future accuser, to be suspected even of a prevarication of preaching towards God. But, on the contrary, concerning the unity of preaching, which we read above, they had joined right hands, and had agreed upon the distribution of duties in the fellowship of the gospel. Just as also elsewhere: whether I or they, so we preach. But even if he described certain false brothers who had crept in, who wanted to transfer the Galatians to another gospel, he himself shows that this adultery of the gospel did not have the intention of transferring to the faith of another God and Christ, but of preserving the discipline of the law, detecting those who were vindicating and observing circumcision, and times and days and months and years of Jewish ceremonies, which they ought to have known were already excluded, according to the renewed disposition of the Creator, who had previously preached this very thing through his prophets, as through Isaiah: the old things have passed away, behold, I am doing new things. And so also through Jeremiah: and I will make a covenant, not like the one I made with your fathers, when I led them out of the land of Egypt; and elsewhere: renew a newness for yourselves, and be circumcised to your God, and circumcise the foreskins of your hearts. Therefore, the apostle, now establishing this circumcision and this newness, was also dissuading those old ceremonies, about which the same Creator of them had once professed that they would cease, through Hosea: and I will turn away all her delights and her feast days and new moons and sabbaths and all her ceremonies. For so also through Isaiah: I do not endure your new moons and sabbaths and great days, your festivals and fasts and feast days, my soul hates. But if the Creator had already rejected all these things long ago, and the apostle was now pronouncing them to be rejected, the very sentence of the apostle, consistent with the decrees of the Creator, proves that the apostle did not preach another God than the one whose decrees he desired to be recognized, noting false apostles and brothers in this cause, who would transfer the gospel of Christ the Creator from the newness foretold by the Creator to the antiquity rejected by the Creator.

pass_b_english: We also need to defend that very clear proof against the clamor of the opposing side. They claim Marcion didn't so much innovate the rule by separating Law and Gospel as revert to a rule previously adulterated. Oh Christ, most patient Lord, you endured the perversion of your preaching for so many years, until Marcion finally came to your rescue! They even pit Peter and the other pillars of the apostleship against Paul, because Paul rebuked them for not walking straight toward the truth of the Gospel. This is the same Paul who was still raw in grace and trembling lest he had run or would run in vain when he first conferred with the earlier apostles. So if, while still burning with zeal like a new convert, he judged something in their conduct reprehensible toward Judaism, then—once convinced—he would later become all things to all men to win them all: to Jews as a Jew, to those under the Law as under the Law. You want that rebuke of mere conduct—a rebuke that would please his future accuser—to be suspected as a falsification of his preaching toward God. But on the contrary, concerning the unity of preaching we read above, they joined right hands and agreed on a division of duties in the fellowship of the Gospel. As Paul says elsewhere: "Whether I or they, so we preach." Even when he describes certain false brothers who slipped in to divert the Galatians to a different gospel, he shows that this adulteration of the Gospel did not aim at transferring faith to another God and Christ, but at preserving the discipline of the Law—detecting those who insisted on circumcision and on observing times, days, months, and years of Jewish ceremonies. They should have known these were already excluded, according to the renewed disposition of the Creator, who had long before preached this very thing through his prophets. Through Isaiah: "The old things have passed away; behold, I am doing new things" (Isaiah 43:19). And through Jeremiah: "I will make a covenant, not like the one I made with your fathers when I led them out of Egypt" (Jeremiah 31:32). And elsewhere: "Renew a newness for yourselves, and be circumcised to your God, and circumcise the foreskins of your hearts." Therefore the apostle, now establishing this circumcision and this newness, was also dissuading those old ceremonies—ceremonies whose own Creator had once declared would cease. Through Hosea: "I will turn away all her delights, her feast days, new moons, sabbaths, and all her ceremonies" (Hosea 2:13). For so also through Isaiah: "I do not endure your new moons and sabbaths and great days; your festivals and fasts and feast days my soul hates." But if the Creator had already rejected all these things long ago, and the apostle now pronounced them rejected, the apostle's own verdict—consistent with the Creator's decrees—proves he did not preach another God than the one whose decrees he wanted recognized. He brands as false both the apostles and the brothers in this cause who would transfer the Gospel of Christ the Creator from the newness foretold by the Creator to the antiquity rejected by the Creator.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex Latin syntax, particularly the long conditional/concessive structure regarding Paul's conduct. Scripture citations added in Pass B (Isaiah 43:19, Jeremiah 31:32, Hosea 2:13) are correct and required by the rules. All clauses in the Locked Latin are accounted for in both Pass A and B.
